newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - NEW ZEALAND NEWSPAPERS - AUG 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NEW ZEALAND NEWSPAPERS - AUG 13.

text.p: Bolger keeps options open: Prime Minister Jim Bolger has left open the option of offering a ministerial post to sole United NZ MP Peter Dunne in a bid to safeguard the government's one-seat majority against any future departure by NZ First list MP Neil Kirton. Page 1.
Elder seeks report on paedophile warnings: Police Minister Jack Elder has asked for a report on British plans to give police powers to warn the public about paedophiles. Page 1.

Bolger hints surtax likely in future accord: Any attempt to revive the superannuation accord after September's retirement savings referendum would have to include some form of income testing on New Zealand superannuation, Prime Minister Jim Bolger indicated on Tuesday. Page 2.

Luxton seeks more asset privatisation: The privatisation of government-owned activities, including local government assets, needed to be considered, Associate Agriculture Minister John Luxton said on Tuesday. Page 2.
What Winebox inquiry lawyers were paid: The government has paid Winebox inquiry lawyers and accountants nearly $5 million, according to Internal Affairs Minister Jack Elder. Page 9.
NZ loses world crown in reading: One in five children fails: About 20 percent of New Zealand children are reading below their age level, and half of those are at least three years behind.
Winebox findngs out tomorrow: Sir Ronald Davison's winebox inquiry report is finished -- and its contents will be revealed on Thursday.

Morris tipped as top contender for health: The Minister of Youth Affairs, Deborah Morris, is being tipped as a leading contender to fill the vacancy created by Neil Kirton's sacking as Associate Minister of Health.

AMP mulls banking licence: AMP says it is likely to join the select group of financial institutions holding a New Zealand banking licence, although a decision to apply for one is not a foregone conclusion.
Intel shows video phone system: Intel Corporation, the world's largest microchip maker, market the official opening of its New Zealand sales and marketing office with a new PC-based video phone.
Smog plan gets council go-ahead: Incentives to help Christchurch people install less polluting forms of heating and improve home insulation will be provided by the city council. Page 1.
TR Pac confident on Asia: TR Pacific Investment Trust said that recent uncertainties in Asian currency markets had produced attractive investment opportunities. Page 31.
Iddison's BTNZ venture on target: Iddison Group Vietnam expects its concrete products joint venture to start production in November. Page 31.

NGC holders opt for shares: Most holders of Natural Gas Corporation's 420 million convertible notes have opted to convert them to shares rather than cash at $1 a note, the natural gas distributor said. Page 30.
